physicalNotes: Radius 0.12195578 Jupiter radii from Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...667A..59D/abstract): 8,718.9 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...667A..59D/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.0796027 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DELREZ_ET_AL_2022): P 8.457463 d
sources.shape: Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DELREZ_ET_AL_2022): a/R* 55.94; Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DELREZ_ET_AL_2022): inclination 89.287 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Delrez et al. 2022 (2022A&A...667A..59D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DELREZ_ET_AL_2022): transit mid-time 2459520.70598 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 6 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
